subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should OpenClaw expose these three independently opt-in pre-handshake Gateway security controls as a supported long-term configuration contract, rather than relying only on the existing origin and trusted-proxy policy paths?
rationale: The patch creates new operator-visible security behavior and defaults; correctness evidence does not determine the desired product security posture or ongoing support surface.

options.title: Adopt the opt-in contract
options.body: Correct the contradictory default wording, document all three settings and deployment prerequisites, then review the enabled and default compatibility paths.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Keep only the hardening that fits the established trusted-proxy or origin policy and remove the remaining new configuration surface.

options.title: Pause for security design
options.body: Defer the PR until Gateway owners define a single supported reverse-proxy and browser-WebSocket threat-model contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Correct the contradictory default wording, document all three settings and deployment prerequisites, then review the enabled and default compatibility paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The available timeline identifies steipete as the closest visible participant for the Gateway-area decision, though code-history ownership could not be confirmed in this sandbox.
